events.quote: Right: "is". Well remembered.
for a plan, use am, is or are + going to + verb
Right: I am going to visit my aunt. Wrong: I going to visit my aunt.
Right: "I ate a sandwich because I was hungry.". Well remembered.
choose the joining word by meaning: and adds an idea, but shows a contrast, because gives a reason
Right: I was tired, but I went to school. Wrong: I was tired and I went to school and I was happy.
one thing (a singular countable noun) always needs a or an
Use an before a vowel sound (an apple) and a before a consonant sound (a cat).
Right: My brother is a doctor. Wrong: My brother is doctor.
Right: "The nurse works in the hospital.". Well remembered.
job and workplace words have fixed spellings with all their vowels
Right: A doctor works in a hospital. Wrong: A doctr works in a hospitl.
Right: "The bus trip is two hours and fifteen minutes.". Well remembered.
Right: "The bus trip is two hours and fifteen minutes.". Well remembered.
number words have fixed spellings: five, fifteen, fifty (f and v are different letters)
An hour is sixty minutes; a clock is the thing on the wall. We say "for one hour", not "one clock".
Right: The lesson is one hour long. Wrong: The lesson is one clock long.
use "the" when we already know which thing ... Do not use "the" with general ideas
Right: I bought a book. The book is very good. Wrong: I bought a book. Book is very good.
Right: I always go to school by bus. Wrong: I go always to school by bus.
Right: "The bathroom is next to the bedroom.". Well remembered.
Right: "The bathroom is next to the bedroom.". Well remembered.
rooms have fixed English names with all their vowels
We do not translate the Arabic phrase: a bedroom, not "a sleeping room".
Right: My kitchen is small. Wrong: My kitchn is small.
Right: "Listen! The baby is crying now.". Well remembered.
Right: "Listen! The baby is crying now.". Well remembered.
for an action happening now, use am, is or are + verb-ing: ... not "He watching TV"
use am, is or are + verb-ing ... and not "He watches TV now"
Right: He is watching TV now. Wrong: He watching TV now.

events.quote: there are + more than one thing, and the plural noun takes -s
"There" always needs is or are after it.
Right: There is a cat in the garden. Wrong: There a cat in the garden.

errors.W1: There are four cup on the table.
errors.W2: There four cups on the table.
